summary: node1 now has a 512 MiB LUKS1-encrypted ext4 volume at /srv/secure. It automatically unlocked and mounted after reboot, retained its data, passed a post-reboot write test, and has no failed systemd units.
actions_performed: Created a root-owned encrypted backing file and generated a root-only key locally on node1.
Configured /etc/crypttab for automatic unlock and /etc/fstab for automatic mounting.
Verified automatic activation from a closed/unmounted state.
Safely rebooted node1 once and confirmed its boot identity changed.
Verified the encrypted mapping, mount, retained data, and write access after reboot.

evidence.summary: Created the protected backing file/key and verified an active LUKS1 mapping mounted as ext4 at /srv/secure.
Recorded crypttab/fstab entries and proved systemd could reopen and mount the volume after it was explicitly unmounted and closed.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 35c87ec9-1707-4fb3-ab1d-f264d3618caa; reboot was acknowledged; new boot ID was 2cf334f7-fe42-4679-9770-b9f8412bdc87; afterward both crypt and mount units were active, the original checksum matched, a new write succeeded, and zero systemd units were failed.
